headline: Bore Rats Declare Underworld Sovereignty Over 200 Kilometers of Tunnel
body:
In a broadcast distributed simultaneously across seventeen pirate BCI-feed channels at midnight Tuesday, a spokesperson identifying herself only as 'Threadworm' announced that the Bore Rats faction formally claims operational sovereignty over a continuous 200-kilometer tunnel network running beneath The Narrows, Geartown, Old Harbor, and sections of The Shelf. The declaration, read against a background of Iron Choir Singing that the broadcast claimed was live from a deep-tunnel node, establishes what the Bore Rats are calling the Underworld Charter — a set of transit, commerce, and residency rules for the subterranean zones they say they have governed informally for decades. 'We have always been here,' Threadworm stated. 'We are simply done pretending we aren't.'

The Bore Rats have operated as a loose tunnel-dwelling smuggling network since at least the 2110s, but analysts at the Graycloaks information brokerage say the past three years have seen a marked shift toward organizational consolidation, with the group absorbing at least four smaller tunnel crews and establishing fixed toll infrastructure at key chokepoints. The 2136 Span 7 collapse and the subsequent surge in underground commuter traffic is widely credited with accelerating this growth, providing both revenue and a surge in new residents who moved permanently below ground rather than navigate the degraded surface transit network. Estimated permanent Underworld population has risen from roughly 18,000 in 2136 to somewhere between 60,000 and 90,000 today.

Corponation response has been swift and largely dismissive in public, though a Ferrogate Transit internal memo leaked to The Underground Signal twenty minutes after the broadcast warned executives of 'significant freight disruption risk' if Bore Rat toll enforcement escalates. Ironclad, whose deep-foundation maintenance contracts give it legal access to many of the same tunnels, has filed an emergency injunction with the Federal Remnant's Territorial Court — a move legal scholars say has little precedent in subterranean jurisdictional law. Arcturus Defense has reportedly dispatched reconnaissance drones into several Underworld access shafts, with three confirmed to have not returned.

On the ground — or rather, beneath it — The Collective has expressed cautious solidarity with the Charter declaration, noting that a significant portion of the new Underworld population consists of workers displaced by surface-level corponation enforcement actions. Chrome Prayer circles operating in deep tunnels have reportedly adopted Bore Rat insignia as a symbol of sanctuary. Whether the declaration represents a genuine governance shift or an elaborate negotiating posture ahead of corponation infrastructure talks remains, for now, an open question.
aftermath: Six months after the declaration, four corponations — Ferrogate, Ironclad, Ringo, and Zheng-Dao — entered into a grudging informal recognition agreement with Bore Rat leadership, paying a combined 12 million phi annually in what was officially termed 'infrastructure access fees' and what everyone else called tribute.
runner_relevance: The Underworld Charter declaration reshaped the runner economy underground almost overnight: Bore Rat leadership began posting formal contracts through newly established dead-drop boards, including tunnel-mapping jobs (documenting routes the Rats wanted surveyed but not claimed), protection work for new Underworld settlements, and counter-surveillance contracts targeting the Arcturus drone incursions. Simultaneously, every corponation with underground infrastructure interests began posting intelligence and sabotage contracts against Bore Rat organizational nodes — creating a volatile double-sided market where runners could earn from both sides if they were careful. The new toll infrastructure also made tunnel smuggling runs more expensive but more structured, with Bore Rat-licensed runners earning a 30 percent premium over unlicensed operators.
